translationRepairs: "Front Brook," by Jin General of Chariots and Cavalry Shen Kuang;
"Front Brook," by Jin General of Chariots and Cavalry Shen Chong;
Chinese 沈珫 gives the personal name Shen Chong (珫 chōng); Kuang is a wrong reading. The proposed idiomatic line corrects only that given name.
"Front Brook" was composed by Jin General of Chariots and Cavalry Shen Kuang;
"Front Brook" was composed by Jin General of Chariots and Cavalry Shen Chong;
Chinese 沈珫 is Shen Chong (珫 chōng); the literal's Shen Kuang is the same misreading. The proposed replacement restores Chong and leaves the rest unchanged.
"Chief Clerk Variation," by Jin Left Chief Clerk Wang Yin;
"Chief Clerk Variation," by Jin Left Chief Clerk Wang Xin;
Chinese 王廞 is Wang Xin (廞 xīn); Yin is a wrong reading of the given name. The proposed idiomatic line corrects only that name.
"Chief Clerk Variation" was composed by Jin Left Chief Clerk of the Minister Wang Yin;
"Chief Clerk Variation" was composed by Jin Left Chief Clerk of the Minister Wang Xin;
Chinese 王廞 is Wang Xin (廞 xīn); the literal's Wang Yin is the same misreading. The proposed replacement restores Xin without other changes.
"Xiangyang," by Song Prince of Sui Wang Dan;
"Xiangyang," by Song Prince of Sui Dan;
Chinese 宋隨王誕 is Song Prince of Sui Dan: 王 is the princely title in 隨王, and 誕 is the personal name. "Wang Dan" wrongly treats 王 as a surname; dropping Wang restores the Chinese.

At the Supreme Clarity Palace's completion Wei Yun, Director of Court Music, offered six pieces—Jingyun, Nine Perfections, Purple Pole, Little Longevity, Receiving Heaven, Following Heaven—and a shang-mode suite, Ruler and Minister Meeting in Joy.

At the Supreme Clarity Palace's completion Wei Tao, Director of Court Music, offered six pieces—Jingyun, Nine Perfections, Purple Pole, Little Longevity, Receiving Heaven, Following Heaven—and a shang-mode suite, Ruler and Minister Meeting in Joy.
Chinese 韋縚 is Wei Tao (縚 tāo); Yun is a wrong reading. The proposed idiomatic line corrects only that personal name.

When the Supreme Clarity Palace was completed, Court Director Wei Yun composed six tunes—"Jingyun," "Nine Perfections," "Purple Pole," "Little Longevity," "Receiving Heaven," and "Following Heaven Music"—and also composed the shang-mode tune "Ruler and Minister Meeting in Joy."

When the Supreme Clarity Palace was completed, Court Director Wei Tao composed six tunes—"Jingyun," "Nine Perfections," "Purple Pole," "Little Longevity," "Receiving Heaven," and "Following Heaven Music"—and also composed the shang-mode tune "Ruler and Minister Meeting in Joy."
Chinese 韋縚 is Wei Tao (縚 tāo); the literal's Wei Yun is the same misreading. The proposed replacement restores Tao and leaves the rest intact.
After Daizong retook the capitals with Prince of Guangping, Pear Garden officer Liu Rijin offered eighteen Precious Response Long Peace pieces, all in palace mode.
When Daizong, as Prince of Guangping, recovered the two capitals, Pear Garden officer Liu Rijin offered eighteen Precious Response Long Peace pieces, all in palace mode.

Chinese 代宗繇廣平王復二京 uses 繇 "from/as" so Daizong, from his prior title Prince of Guangping, recovered the two capitals—one person, not Daizong together with another Prince of Guangping. The proposed idiomatic wording restores that identity.
Xuanzong's ministerial banquets always featured the full hundred acts.
Xuānzong's ministerial banquets always featured the full hundred acts.
Chinese 宣宗 is Xuānzong, not the better-known 玄宗 (Xuánzong); undiacriticized Xuanzong conflates the two. Context (大中) confirms 宣宗, and the proposed tone-marked Xuānzong correctly disambiguates.
